overview: This file documents U.S. State and War Department deliberations from February through June 1947 over restoring and regulating Japan’s international communications under the Allied occupation. Most of the papers concern categories of telegrams payable in yen, allocation of foreign-currency receipts, and negotiations with Britain over the London–Osaka radiotelegraph circuit; related documents address the Danish Great Northern Telegraph Company’s proposed Nagasaki relay station and the Shanghai–Nagasaki–Vladivostok cable route. The final memorandum broadens the subject to transactional mail, informational mail, and SCAP’s proposed relaxation of postal censorship.

subfiles.title: Martin memorandum on draft cable to SCAP concerning yen-prepaid telegrams
subfiles.about: Explains and recommends a proposed response to SCAP on permissible yen-prepaid messages and international accounting arrangements.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum reviews SCAP’s proposal to limit yen-prepaid outbound traffic to Expeditionary Force Messages and Sender’s Composition Messages, while suggesting continued consideration of messages promoting Japanese foreign trade. It rejects a sender-take-all settlement system because restricted outbound traffic would disadvantage Japanese carriers. It also supports offsetting British claims for yen collections against sterling balances arising from British traffic on the prospective London–Osaka circuit.

subfiles.title: Moreland recommendation for approval of Japanese telecommunications cable
subfiles.about: Recommends approval of a cable addressing message categories and financial settlement for Japan’s international telecommunications.
subfiles.summary: Moreland summarizes the exchange with SCAP over the categories of telegrams that could be prepaid in yen. The proposed cable also asks about British negotiations concerning financial settlement and reopening the London–Osaka circuit. He notes Colonel Dice’s concurrence and recommends Hilldring’s approval.

subfiles.title: Moreland request to Colonel Chard for War Department concurrence
subfiles.about: Requests War Department concurrence in a draft cable on yen-prepaid traffic and British settlement arrangements.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum explains SCAP’s proposed restriction of yen-prepaid messages to EFM and SCM traffic and urges reconsideration of trade-promotion messages. It argues for full accounting between telecommunications administrations and for making Japan’s net foreign-currency earnings available for imports. Moreland endorses Britain’s preference to offset yen liabilities against sterling balances and asks Colonel Chard to secure War Department concurrence.

subfiles.title: Moreland memorandum on the United Kingdom–Japan radiotelegraph service
subfiles.about: Reviews policy and British proposals for reopening the London–Osaka radiotelegraph circuit.
subfiles.summary: Moreland reports SCAP’s inquiry into the status of discussions with Britain and reiterates that SCAP should conduct the actual negotiations. He considers acceptable the British proposal to handle only prepaid-into-Japan and collect-from-Japan messages for the time being. He recommends that Japanese carriers’ foreign-exchange earnings be available for trade and notes that Colonel Dice has provided War Department concurrence.

subfiles.title: Moreland memorandum to Hilldring on the Great Northern Telegraph Company
subfiles.about: Seeks concurrence in asking SCAP about the Great Northern Telegraph Company’s application to restore its Nagasaki cable relay station.
subfiles.summary: The Danish company wished to connect its Shanghai–Nagasaki and Nagasaki–Vladivostok submarine cables at a minimally staffed relay station. The proposed cable asks SCAP for the status of the application so that the American Embassy in Copenhagen can be answered. Moreland records War Department concurrence and notes that Copenhagen was being informed of the referral.

subfiles.title: Moreland memorandum to the War Department on the Nagasaki relay station
subfiles.from: Mr. Moreland, A-H, Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards a proposed inquiry concerning restoration of the Great Northern Telegraph Company relay station at Nagasaki.
subfiles.summary: This covering memorandum describes the Danish company’s limited proposal to join its Shanghai–Nagasaki and Nagasaki–Vladivostok cables and maintain equipment for relaying, testing, and balancing signals. The attached inquiry was intended to establish the status of the company’s application and provide the basis for a reply to the American Embassy at Copenhagen.

subfiles.title: Draft telegram to SCAP requesting status of the Nagasaki station
subfiles.about: Requests immediate information on when the Great Northern Telegraph Company may resume its Nagasaki relay service.
subfiles.summary: The brief telegram informs SCAP that the Department learned through the Embassy at Copenhagen of the company’s request to reestablish its Nagasaki cable relay station. It asks for information as soon as possible on when the service may resume.

subfiles.title: Moreland memorandum accepting SCAP’s interim telecommunications policy
subfiles.about: Endorses SCAP’s uniform payment policy while reserving the issue of yen-prepaid trade messages for later reconsideration.
subfiles.summary: SCAP proposed treating all countries alike and permitting yen-prepaid outbound messages only in the EFM and SCM categories for accredited personnel. Moreland accepts that position temporarily but recommends revisiting trade-related telegrams when private trade resumes. He also concurs that a British plan to convert certain yen receipts into sterling is undesirable and urges treatment comparable to that applied to U.S. personnel.

subfiles.title: McDiarmid memorandum transferring action on SCAP cable C-51680
subfiles.about: Transfers responsibility for answering SCAP’s cable on message-payment rules and British settlement arrangements.
subfiles.summary: McDiarmid interprets SCAP’s policy as placing all countries on the same payment basis and restricting yen-prepaid outbound messages to EFM and SCM traffic. He recommends accepting the policy until private trade resumes. Regarding the London–Osaka circuit, he finds some merit in SCAP’s objection to Britain’s proposed offsetting arrangement but recommends examining U.S. practice and placing the United Kingdom on a comparable basis.

subfiles.title: Whitman memorandum and draft telegram on relaxation of mail communications
subfiles.about: Proposes an interim response asking SCAP to reconsider relaxation of postal censorship in light of policy on transactional mail.
subfiles.summary: Whitman notes that SCAP’s proposal to relax mail restrictions crossed with a U.S. cable concerning transactional mail. The draft reply argues that the definition and admission of transactional communications will affect the scale and character of censorship. It asks SCAP to reconsider discontinuing complete censorship and recommends that any press release address both expanded informational mail and the reopening of transactional mail.

interest: The file is especially useful for showing how seemingly technical communications policy intersected with occupation finance, Japanese trade recovery, currency convertibility, and relations among the United States, Britain, Denmark, and SCAP. Its layered memoranda reveal the bureaucratic route by which State and War Department officials developed, cleared, and transmitted policy. The Nagasaki papers illuminate efforts to reconnect prewar submarine-cable infrastructure, while the final item shows censorship policy being reconsidered as Japan’s commercial and informational contacts with the outside world reopened.
